references.text: Mentions Aroer by the bank of the Arnon River as the boundary of the land Israel conquered from Sihon, the same geographical reference point as in Deuteronomy 4:48.
Describes the conquest of the land from the Arnon River to Mount Hermon, and notes that the Sidonians call Hermon Sirjon, showing the connection with Zion/Sirjon in 4:48.
Summarizes the territory Israel conquered east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon, the same geographical area described in Deuteronomy 4:48.
Describes the area from Aroer by the Arnon River and includes Mount Hermon, the same boundary region mentioned in Deuteronomy 4:48.
Mentions the Arnon as the border between Moab and the Amorites, the same river that marks the southern boundary in Deuteronomy 4:48.
Mentions Mount Hermon as an important geographical location in Israel, the same mountain identified with Zion in Deuteronomy 4:48.
